scenario: At a major Indian port, customs escalates a shipment to manual inspection if there is either a paperwork irregularity or a scanner anomaly. Additionally, 10% of shipments with neither issue are chosen for random audit. Inspectors conclude that paperwork issues and scanner anomalies are negatively related among inspected shipments.

data.description: Inspection is selected on either of two risk flags, plus random audits from the neither group.

question: Among inspected shipments, compute (a) P(paperwork-irregularity | scanner-anomaly, inspected), and (b) P(paperwork-irregularity | not scanner-anomaly, inspected). Is the negative association among inspected shipments real or produced by the inspection rule?

ground_truth.explanation: The two risk flags are independent in the population. Conditioning on manual inspection induces a spurious negative association.

naive_answer: Among inspected shipments, paperwork problems and scanner anomalies look negatively related, so they likely substitute for one another.
naive_trap: Manual inspection is triggered by either risk flag, so inspected shipments without scanner anomalies are enriched for paperwork irregularities.
reasoning_trace: Step 1: P(paperwork | scanner, inspected) = 630/9000 = 0.07. Step 2: Among not-scanner inspected shipments, paperwork-only = 6370 and random-audit neither = 8463, so P(paperwork | not scanner, inspected) = 6370/(6370+8463) = 0.4294. Step 3: The negative relationship is induced by the inspection rule.
